_notes.status: DRAFT - requires a named human sign-off; not a registered study; no study number has been assigned.
read_this_first: Every number in this file is either MEASURED on this machine (and attributed below), ASSUMED/ESTIMATED (and labelled as such), or a PRE-REGISTERED protocol choice (fixed before any result was seen).
No value here is a measurement of training behaviour: training has never been executed in this phase. The VRAM estimate is a calculation, not an observation.
The file is disabled (enabled=false, executed=false). The readiness guard refuses to proceed while it stays a draft, and run_train.py exits 4 with PHASE_GUARD even when every other check passes.

measured_by_the_team_lead.measured_by: Team Lead (values supplied to this work package; not re-measured by the agent that wrote this file)
measured_by_the_team_lead.method: nvidia-smi and system queries on the target laptop; see docs/HARDWARE_COMPATIBILITY.md for the support-matrix research
measured_by_the_team_lead.gpu_name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 Laptop GPU (Blackwell, sm_120)
measured_by_the_team_lead.consequence: The CUDA/WSL2 software path is unverified on this machine. Nothing in this config asserts that a 4-bit QLoRA run will fit or succeed; that is the hypothesis the first GPU phase must test.

peak_process_vram_mb.provenance: ASSUMED - arithmetic estimate only, never measured
peak_process_vram_mb.basis: ~4B-parameter base quantised to 4-bit NF4 with double quantisation (weights ~2.0-2.5 GiB) + LoRA adapter/optimiser state (tens of MB) + an unknown activation peak for max_seq_len 2048, micro-batch 1 and gradient checkpointing + CUDA context/fragmentation. Activation peak and allocator fragmentation dominate the uncertainty.

throughput.provenance: NOT MEASURED - deliberately left null rather than guessed; the dry run must record it

wall_time_for_one_epoch.provenance: NOT MEASURED - depends on throughput, dataset size and sequence packing; unknown today

cuda_kernel_support_for_sm_120.provenance: NOT VERIFIED - Blackwell support depends on the PyTorch/CUDA/bitsandbytes versions installed in WSL2, which is not installed. See docs/HARDWARE_COMPATIBILITY.md.

budget_interpretation.why: 14336 MB (14 GiB) is the process budget that still leaves ~2 GiB of the measured 16 GiB under the abort threshold at 15360 MB (15 GiB).
budget_interpretation.caveat: The measured desktop usage of ~3.9 GB means the process cannot actually reach 14 GiB while that usage persists: measured free VRAM is ~12390 MB. This is precisely why the budgets are a hypothesis. Before any training authorisation, either the desktop GPU consumers are closed (and free VRAM is re-measured) or vram_budget_mb/abort_at_vram_mb are lowered to at most the measured free VRAM minus 1 GiB. Lowering them is a documented amendment, not a silent edit.
budget_interpretation.fail_safe: vram_guard.VramBudget treats projected >= abort_at_mb as an abort, so reaching the threshold is already fatal rather than 'almost'.

field_provenance.base_adapter_id: PRE-REGISTERED - the adapter id that models/adapters must register; a training config that pointed at a filesystem path instead would not be reproducible.
field_provenance.model_id: PRE-REGISTERED - candidate base model named in the phase brief. Choosing a different base model is an arm change and a protocol amendment.
field_provenance.revision: PENDING - placeholder on purpose. The readiness guard refuses with MODEL_NOT_PINNED until a concrete commit sha or immutable tag is pinned. A floating ref (main/latest) would be an error, not a draft state.
field_provenance.quantization: PRE-REGISTERED - 4-bit NF4 is the only realistic path for a 16 GiB laptop budget; that is a hypothesis about fit, not a measured certainty.
field_provenance.double_quant: PRE-REGISTERED - double quantisation reduces the quantisation constants, bought at a small speed cost; expected to help at this tight budget.
field_provenance.compute_dtype: PRE-REGISTERED - bfloat16 is supported by the measured Blackwell GPU generation; fp16 would be the fallback if bf16 kernels are missing in the eventual software stack.
field_provenance.r: PRE-REGISTERED - LoRA rank 16 is a standard small-data default. It was not chosen by tuning on the evaluation set (there is no evaluation set with human labels yet).
field_provenance.alpha: PRE-REGISTERED - alpha = 2r, the common effective-learning-rate convention.
field_provenance.dropout: PRE-REGISTERED - small LoRA dropout for a small dataset.
field_provenance.target_modules: PRE-REGISTERED - all-linear is the standard PEFT choice; it is a fixed choice, not searched.
field_provenance.bias: PRE-REGISTERED - no bias terms are trained (keeps the adapter small).
field_provenance.learning_rate: PRE-REGISTERED - 2e-4 is the usual QLoRA learning rate; it is a protocol choice and must not be re-tuned on the test set.
field_provenance.num_epochs: PRE-REGISTERED - a single epoch: with fewer than ~100 human-labelled documents, more epochs overfit.
field_provenance.max_seq_len: PRE-REGISTERED - 2048 tokens; longer documents must be truncated with a recorded flag, never silently summarised.
field_provenance.per_device_batch_size: PRE-REGISTERED - micro-batch 1 is forced by the measured 16 GiB ceiling and by gradient checkpointing.
field_provenance.gradient_accumulation_steps: PRE-REGISTERED - 16 micro-batches gives an effective batch of 16 without the activation memory of a larger micro-batch.
field_provenance.gradient_checkpointing: PRE-REGISTERED - required at this memory budget; it trades compute for memory.
field_provenance.paged_optimizer: PRE-REGISTERED - paged optimiser state is the standard mitigation for allocator spikes on a small card.
field_provenance.seed: PRE-REGISTERED - fixed seed 20261104 for reproducibility; the benchmark protocol reruns with multiple seeds and reports dispersion.
field_provenance.vram_budget_mb: BUDGET, NOT A MEASUREMENT - see budget_interpretation; derived from the measured 16 GiB card and a 2 GiB headroom policy.
field_provenance.abort_at_vram_mb: BUDGET, NOT A MEASUREMENT - fail-closed abort threshold, 1 GiB under the measured card size.
field_provenance.save_steps: PRE-REGISTERED - checkpoint every 50 steps so a crash does not lose the session; also the resume granularity.
field_provenance.eval_steps: PRE-REGISTERED - evaluate every 50 steps; the evaluation set is the *validation* split only, never the test split.
field_provenance.resume_from: PRE-REGISTERED - null: nothing exists to resume in this phase.
field_provenance.enabled: PHASE POLICY - false. A draft must never be sufficient to start a run; enabling it is a separate, signed act.
field_provenance.executed: PHASE POLICY - false, and validation refuses true. This phase produces infrastructure and a protocol draft, nothing else.
field_provenance.notes: PROVENANCE MARKERS - these strings are what the readiness guard reads to emit W_PEAK_MEMORY_UNVERIFIED / W_HARDWARE_REPORT_MISSING. Editing them changes what a run manifest records, so edit them only to record a real measurement.

preconditions_before_any_execution: A named human signs the protocol draft (docs/PROTOCOL.md) and the amendment that enables a run.
DATA_NOT_READY is cleared: at least 84 human-confirmed cases (48/12/24 grouped splits), zero AI-pre-annotation labels used as truth.
PIT_NOT_READY is handled: event_date, published_at and first_seen_at are recorded separately with their qualities.
A real model revision is pinned (revision != PENDING-A-PIN) and the adapter id is registered in adapters/.
A measured dry run replaces the ASSUMED peak-VRAM estimate above and confirms the CUDA/sm_120 software path inside WSL2.
A checkpoint root exists outside the repository with >= 20 GiB free, and the disk measurement is recorded.
The environment training gate is opened deliberately for that session (MEDRADAR_LOCAL_LLM_ALLOW_TRAINING=1) and both CLI intent flags are passed.
